newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Orange, CAIB bid for Austria GSM licence.
newsitem.headline: Orange, CAIB bid for Austria GSM licence.

text.p: Britain's Orange Plc and Creditanstalt Investment Bank (CAIB) entered the bidding for Austria's third mobile telephone licence ahead of Wednesday's deadline, Creditanstalt said.

The joint bid, in which Creditanstalt has a 51 percent stake, is up against the long standing Connect Austria consortium, which groups Austria's Radex-Heraklith , Germany's Viag , unlisted Constantia Privatbank and bank GiroCredit of Austria.
"I can confirm that CAIB and Orange have lodged a bid and CAIB will have a 51 percent stake," a Creditanstalt spokesman told Reuters. He declined to give further details.

The deadline for bids passed at 1200 GMT. Local news agency APA said the Transport Ministry had received only two bids for the potentially lucrative licence but no-one at the ministry was immediately available to confirm the report.
The ministry was likely to give both bidders an opportunity to up their price next month and award the licence at the end of August, APA said.

In December 1995, Austria's second mobile licence went for four billion schillings to max.mobil -- a consortium comprising Germany's DeTeMobil, the Austrian unit of Siemens and several banking partners.
